title: SpaceX, Tesla to initially spend $16.8 billion on Terafab chip plant in Texas
author: B
text:
Daniel Nenni
Founder
Staff member

SpaceX and Tesla will initially invest $16.8 billion to build Terafab, a semiconductor manufacturing complex in Grimes County, Texas, as Elon Musk’s companies seek control over the advanced chips powering artificial intelligence, autonomous vehicles, robots and space systems.

The companies say the facility will integrate chip design, fabrication, memory production, advanced packaging and testing under one roof. Terafab is intended to address what SpaceX describes as a widening gap between global semiconductor output and the computing needs of Musk’s businesses. Those requirements could eventually exceed one terawatt of power, far beyond current worldwide production capacity.

Texas Governor Greg Abbott said the planned complex would cover about 100 million square feet and create 3,000 jobs. The project would deepen both companies’ presence in Texas: Tesla moved its headquarters to Austin in 2021, while SpaceX relocated its headquarters to Starbase in 2024.

Terafab will follow a research fabrication facility that Tesla began building in April at the north campus of its Giga Texas factory near Austin. That operation is expected to serve as a testing ground for manufacturing processes before they are deployed at much greater scale in Grimes County.

The investment underscores a broader push by technology companies to secure domestic semiconductor supplies amid surging demand for AI computing. Yet building an advanced chip plant at this scale carries technical, financial and execution risks. SpaceX and Tesla will need specialized equipment, experienced engineers, reliable power and water supplies, and years of sustained investment before Terafab can meet its ambitious production targets.
